newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Tightened S.Korean security curbs gold smuggling.
newsitem.headline: Tightened S.Korean security curbs gold smuggling.

text.p: The flow of smuggled gold into South Korea has dried up and bullion prices have risen after internal security was tightened in response to the weekend shooting of a North Korean defector, traders said on Tuesday.
"We haven't seen see any smuggled gold since Monday. It is quite unusal," a bullion dealer with Ssangyong Corp said.
South Korea normally imports an average of about 350 kg of gold a day. An estimated 85 percent of it is smuggled to avoid a three percent import tax and 10 percent value-added tax.
On Tuesday, the local retail price of gold was 41,000 won per 3.75 grams, up from 40,500 won on Friday and 39,200 won a week earlier.
Li Il-nam, a nephew of North Korean leader Kim Jong-il's ex-wife, was shot and seriously wounded at the weekend by suspected North Korean agents near Seoul.
Li, who defected to South Korea in 1982, is currently in a coma and on life support.

On Tuesday, Prime Minister Lee Soo-sung said Li's shooting, following the defection of a top Pyongyang official, reminded South Koreans of the importance of security in the the country and he called for "extraordinary alertness" against the North.
South Korea has placed all its police forces on full alert and tightened customs checks in response to the hightened tensions with its Stalinist neighbour.
"We saw the same situation in the gold market last September when the country was in uproar over the incursion by a North Korean submarine," said a dealer with LG Metals Corp.
Other dealers said they expected South Korean firms to rush to accelerate legal imports of gold and for supplies to retun to normal in about a week.
"We cannot compete with smugglers who are not paying import and value-added taxes," said a trader with one major bullion house who asked not to be identified.

The smugglers normally undercut LG Metals daily selling price for gold, which is the benchmark for the wholesale market, by between two to three percent and can obtain margins of eight percent on their sales.

The LG Metals' gold price was set at 10,100 won a gram on Tuesday from 10,000 won a week ago. The company's silver selling price has also risen by nine won a gram to 163 won in the past week in line with higher international prices.

Key Lee, manager of the Seoul office of the World Gold Council, an industry promotion group, said smuggled gold covered 80 to 85 percent of South Korea's jewellery demand in 1996. He said the country'sd total gold demand was 125.5 tonnes last year compared with 121 tonnes in 1995.
The jewellery sector accounted for 110 tonnes of total gold demand in 1996 against 104 tonnes in the previous year.
The remaining portion was for investment, Lee added.
